title: Selected binding coverage: which check pins each consumed source? (scoped adversarial audit, no new kappa)
body:
## Selected binding coverage: which check pins each consumed source? (no new kappa)

**Scoped adversarial audit of one acceptance obligation.** Adds only `research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342/`. The selected record and all frozen sources are unchanged.

Aaron Wang, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in task selection, implementation, verification and writing; disclosed in `TASK.json`).

- Track: adversarial audit; card `supplier-boundary-audit` (scope key `dcdb0fa8e49b08a958d0`), scope **refined**; chooser seed `a342df779f61a21ef22797b2d9816a0e`, priority revision 3.
- Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`.
- Branch: `research/agent-33-binding-coverage-a342df77`, contribution head `3d54b62b` on that base.

## Question

The selected record's `source_manifest` inventory check ("Selected package inventory or bytes changed") is what binds the audited supplier sources. Does that obligation — the audited sources are the consumed sources — follow from the actual source-bound checks of the acceptance path?

## Result

For every repository input consumed by the selected fast acceptance (`scripts/verify_selected_result.py`) and the documented reproduce driver (`scripts/verify_frontier1094.py`, including its `--baseline1042` reuse mode and the frozen `research/complex-t16-rare-pattern-exchanges` chain), the package names the check that pins the bytes:

| Binding class | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| manifest-roots inventory (1,579 files, 13 package roots) | 8 |
| record `proof_supplements` digests | 5 |
| record `certificate_sha256` | 1 |
| checkpoint self-binding (`certificates/checkpoints/frontier1042.json` re-enters `check()`) | 1 |
| record root of trust | 1 |
| **NONE** | 4 |

The four unbound consumed inputs, each with a smallest fixture through the real `check()`:

1. `research/community-frontier1094-audit/SELECTED-SOURCE.json` — the inventory anchor itself; the record has no `source_manifest_sha256`. Fixture: a semantically invalid but superficially well-formed forgery that changes one inventory file **and** the manifest digest list consistently is **accepted**.
2. `scripts/verify_selected_result.py` — the acceptance checker's own bytes are pinned by no record-level check (root-of-trust observation).
3. `research/community-frontier1042-audit/RESULT.json` — the published baseline receipt that the `--baseline1042` reuse mode compares its supplied work directory against; the comparison target is unbound at record level (its *claims* remain constrained downstream: stage list, kappa constant, and recorded script hashes checked against live repository scripts).
4. `docs/research/community-batch1099-integration.json` — existence-only publication pointer by documented design.

Bound mutations are rejected with their exact errors (`Selected package inventory or bytes changed`, `Selected proof supplement changed`, `Selected primary proof is not covered by a verified digest`, `Selected decimal differs from exact kappa`); existence-only and unbound-sidecar mutations are accepted, as the documentation states. So the source-binding obligation holds for the entire frozen supplier payload (all 1,579 manifest files, both upstream archives via package MANIFEST self-pins, the five pinned harness scripts) and fails only at the four anchors above. No certificate, supplier, or frontier value is affected.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342/verify.py
```

Expected final line: `PASS_SELECTED_BINDING_COVERAGE_AUDIT unbound=4 fixtures=7` (about 3 s).

Registered replay and metadata check both pass on Python 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342 --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342
```

Output: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)`, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-binding-coverage-seeda342 outcome=completed`. Also run green on Python 3.13 and 3.12 standalone.

## Method and controls

- Consumed set enumerated from the pinned scripts' literal path reads and subprocess calls; a control regex-scans both pinned scripts for path literals resolving to repository files and requires every one to sit inside the enumeration or `proof_supplements` (remainder is empty and recorded).
- Fixtures run the imported production `check()` in a temporary directory; the working tree is read-only; the deterministic receipt is compared to `EXPECTED.json`.
- Entry overlap refresh at 2026-10-14 12:00–12:01 UTC: `scripts/find_overlap.py` with the refined object terms (`manifest coverage`, `source inventory`, `SELECTED-SOURCE`, `coverage law`, `source binding`, `package roots`), 519 open PRs and 488 discussion records, complete pagination. No matches is not a novelty proof.

## Limitations and remaining obligations

- Not checked: any mathematical supplier obligation, the full cold replay (`make frontier1094-verify`; the documented command is a make target and `make` is not installed on this host — the underlying `scripts/verify_frontier1094.py` stages were read, not run), CI, and any proposed record change.
- The enumeration covers the fast acceptance and documented reproduce driver; frozen-chain internals are classified by their package pins, not line-audited.
- Any fix (e.g. `source_manifest_sha256`) needs maintainer authorization to change the selected record and its acceptance script; both are pinned inputs of many packages.

## Credit and overlap

- Method: `research/owner-boundary-audit` (Tekalign) — trace one obligation, then try to break it with one fixture.
- `research/selected-source-coverage-audit` (seed 97 consolidation note) maps *review* coverage of `source_prs` against the PR ledger; this package asks which check pins the *bytes* of each consumed input, with fixtures against the live acceptance function.
- `research/frontier1094-ancestry-binding-seed69` (Sagar Thakrar) reproduces the [PR 799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799)/[PR 741](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/741) ancestry binding through `check_selected`; that binding is counted here as `checkpoint-self-binding` and not re-audited.
- `research/retained-bit-supplier-binding` guards bit-supplier identity across committed assemblies; untouched here.
- Fresh claims checked at entry (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166): none claim this object; the `supplier-boundary-audit` card's prior use (compact dirty-control agreement set, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1823) is a different object and is complete.
